items.title: Added a warning when the requested model is deprecated or automatically updated to a newer model, shown on stderr in print mode (-p) and now also…

explanation.what_it_is: A warning is now displayed when a requested model is deprecated or has been automatically updated to a newer version.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change helps Claude Code users stay informed about model updates and deprecations, allowing them to adjust their workflows accordingly.
how_to_use: Run Claude Code with the print mode flag (-p) to see the warning on stderr.
Check the warning to determine if your requested model has been updated or deprecated.

items.title: Added attribution.sessionUrl setting to omit the claude.ai session link from commits and PRs in web and Remote Control sessions

explanation.what_it_is: The attribution.sessionUrl setting allows you to control whether the Claude Code session link is included in commits and pull requests. This setting applies to both web and Remote Control sessions.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting gives you more control over the information included in your commits and PRs, which can be useful for maintaining a clean and organized project history.
how_to_use: Set attribution.sessionUrl to false to omit the session link from commits and PRs
Use this setting in web sessions to keep your project history free of unnecessary links
Apply this setting in Remote Control sessions to maintain consistency with your web session settings

items.title: Added /config --help to list all available shorthand keys for /config key=value

explanation.what_it_is: The /config command now supports a --help option, which lists all available shorthand keys for configuring key-value pairs.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update makes it easier for users to discover and use the available shorthand keys, streamlining their configuration workflow.
how_to_use: Run /config --help to view a list of all supported shorthand keys
Use the listed shorthand keys to configure key-value pairs, e.g., /config k=v

items.title: Added /config key=value syntax to set any setting from the prompt (e.g. /config thinking=false) — works in interactive, -p, and Remote Control

explanation.what_it_is: The /config key=value syntax allows you to set any Claude Code setting directly from the prompt. This syntax can be used in interactive mode, with the -p flag, or in Remote Control.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives you more flexibility and control over your Claude Code settings, as you can now change them on the fly without having to navigate through menus or configuration files. This can streamline your workflow and reduce the time spent on configuration.
how_to_use: /config thinking=false to disable thinking mode
/config verbose=true to enable verbose output
/config timeout=300 to set a 5-minute timeout

items.title: Added sandbox.allowAppleEvents opt-in setting that lets sandboxed commands send Apple Events on macOS

explanation.what_it_is: The sandbox.allowAppleEvents setting is an opt-in feature that allows sandboxed commands in Claude Code to send Apple Events on macOS, enabling interaction with other applications on the system.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update matters because it gives developers more control over how their sandboxed commands interact with the macOS environment, allowing for more complex automation workflows.
how_to_use: Enable the sandbox.allowAppleEvents setting in your Claude Code configuration to allow a sandboxed command to send Apple Events to other macOS applications.
Use this setting to automate tasks that require interaction with other applications on the system, such as scripting or automation workflows.

items.title: Added CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE environment variable: point it at a marker file to suppress mobile push notifications while you're at the machine

explanation.what_it_is: The CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE environment variable allows you to specify a marker file that indicates your presence at a machine, which can be used to suppress mobile push notifications.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature matters because it enables you to avoid receiving redundant mobile push notifications when you're already actively working on a machine, reducing notification noise and potential distractions.
how_to_use: Set the CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE environment variable to point to a marker file on your machine, such as a hidden file in your home directory.
Ensure the marker file is updated or touched when you're actively using the machine, so that Claude Code can detect your presence and suppress mobile push notifications.

items.title: Added Tool(param:value) syntax for permission rules to match a tool's input parameters (with * wildcard), e.g. Agent(model:opus) to block Opus…

explanation.what_it_is: The Tool(param:value) syntax allows you to specify permission rules based on a tool's input parameters, with support for wildcard matching using the * character.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables more fine-grained control over tool permissions, allowing you to block or allow specific tools based on their input parameters.
how_to_use: Use Agent(model:opus) to block the Opus model
Use Tool(param:*) to match any tool with a specific parameter

items.title: We've retired the Claude Sonnet 4 model (claude-sonnet-4-20250514) and the…
items.summary: We've retired the Claude Sonnet 4 model (claude-sonnet-4-20250514) and the Claude Opus 4 model (claude-opus-4-20250514). All requests to these models will now return an error. We recommend upgrading…

explanation.what_it_is: The Claude Sonnet 4 and Claude Opus 4 models have been retired, and any requests to these models will now return an error.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change requires users to upgrade to newer models to continue using the Claude API, as the retired models are no longer supported.
how_to_use: Update your API requests to use the latest available models
Check the Anthropic API documentation for recommended replacement models

items.title: Added footerLinksRegexes setting for regex-matched link badges in the footer row, configurable via user or managed settings

explanation.what_it_is: The footerLinksRegexes setting allows you to specify regular expressions for matching link badges in the footer row of Claude Code, enabling customizable link display.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting gives users more control over the appearance of links in the footer, allowing for more tailored and organized displays of relevant information.
how_to_use: Configure the footerLinksRegexes setting via user settings to display specific links in the footer
Use managed settings to apply the footerLinksRegexes configuration across multiple users or teams

items.title: Added enforceAvailableModels managed setting — when enabled, the availableModels allowlist also constrains the Default model (a Default that would…

explanation.what_it_is: The enforceAvailableModels managed setting is a new configuration option that, when enabled, restricts the Default model to only use models specified in the availableModels allowlist.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting gives Claude Code users more control over model usage, ensuring that the Default model only utilizes approved models and preventing unintended model usage.
how_to_use: Enable the enforceAvailableModels setting to enforce model constraints on the Default model
Configure the availableModels allowlist to specify the approved models for the Default model to use

items.title: Added wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled setting to disable mouse-wheel scroll acceleration in fullscreen mode

explanation.what_it_is: The wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled setting allows you to disable mouse-wheel scroll acceleration when Claude Code is in fullscreen mode.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting gives users more control over their scrolling experience, which can be particularly useful for precise tasks or presentations.
how_to_use: Set wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled to false in your Claude Code settings to disable scroll acceleration in fullscreen mode.

items.title: [VSCode] Added usage attribution to the Account & usage dialog (/usage) showing cache misses, long context, subagents, and per-skill/agent/plugin/MCP…

explanation.what_it_is: The Account & usage dialog in VSCode now displays detailed usage attribution, including cache misses, long context, subagents, and per-skill/agent/plugin/MCP usage.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows Claude Code users to better understand their usage patterns and identify potential areas for optimization, such as reducing cache misses or optimizing long context usage.
how_to_use: Open the Account & usage dialog (/usage) to view detailed usage attribution
Use the per-skill/agent/plugin/MCP usage data to identify which components are driving usage
Analyze cache misses and long context usage to optimize your workflow

items.title: The code execution tool now supports code_execution_20260521, which discloses…
items.summary: The code execution tool now supports code_execution_20260521, which discloses the 90-second per-cell execution time limit in the tool description so Claude can budget long-running cells. No beta…

explanation.what_it_is: The code execution tool now supports a feature that discloses the 90-second per-cell execution time limit, allowing Claude to manage long-running cells more effectively.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update helps Claude Code users avoid unexpected timeouts and plan their code execution more efficiently by providing clear information about the execution time limits.
how_to_use: Check the tool description for the 90-second per-cell execution time limit when planning code execution
Use this information to budget time for long-running cells and avoid timeouts

explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to streamline their workflows by excluding already-processed results, reducing unnecessary data transfer and processing.

Use this feature in agentic workflows to improve performance and reduce latency
